data.title: Replay Sports Cards Opens First New York Location, Bringing Community Card Shop to Long Island
data.description:
Replay Sports Cards Opens First New York Location, Bringing Community Card Shop to Long Island

Replay Sports Cards Opens First New York Location, Bringing Community Card Shop to Long Island

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026

Long Island Native Rob Ansalone Debuts Bellmore Shop, Marking Replay's Entrance into New York

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Replay Sports Cards ("Replay"), America's first national franchise dedicated exclusively to the sports card hobby, will open its first New York location on Saturday, November 21, bringing its community-focused approach to buying, selling, trading and grading cards to Long Island. Located at 2156 Bellmore Ave, Bellmore, N.Y. 11710, the new shop is owned by Long Island native Rob Ansalone, who is turning a lifelong passion for sports and collecting into a local gathering place for fans and families.

The opening marks Replay's entrance into New York and extends the brand's reach into one of the country's most passionate sports markets. For Ansalone, a Merrick native, the shop is a chance to give Long Island collectors a dedicated space to connect, trade and share the hobby in a welcoming, community-first environment. The milestone is especially personal for Replay Co-Founder Mike Martin, who grew up in the same community, just minutes from the new shop.

A Lifelong Fan Turns Passion Into a Local Hub

Ansalone spent several years as an insurance broker and previously owned a gym franchise before exploring his next entrepreneurial opportunity. While sports and collecting had always been a passion, his return to the hobby began when he reconnected with the cards he had saved from childhood. Sharing them with his son turned collecting into something the two could enjoy together, and that experience shaped his vision for the Bellmore shop.

"I've loved sports and collecting since I was a kid, but getting back into cards with my son reminded me how special this hobby really is," said Ansalone. "There's a real community of collectors on Long Island, and I wanted to give them a place to come together, trade, and pass the hobby on to the next generation."

Ansalone was drawn to Replay because it gave him a way to enter the card shop business with the support, structure and collaboration of an experienced franchise team rather than building a shop on his own. His shared roots with Martin, who grew up in the same Bellmore/Merrick area, made the opportunity feel personal from the start.

"Opening a Replay shop in my hometown is a true full-circle moment for me," said Martin. "I spent more than 20 years in this community, and the shop is about five minutes from the house I grew up in. Getting to bring one of our shops to the place that shaped me, and to do it alongside someone like Rob who shares those same roots, means the world. This is exactly the kind of place I would have loved to have as a kid."

Growing the Hobby Across New Markets

Replay continues to expand its franchise network by partnering with entrepreneurs who combine a passion for collecting with a commitment to their local communities. Its model brings together buying, selling, trading and grading services with online sales, livestream commerce, and community events, giving collectors multiple ways to engage with the hobby both in-shop and online.

For those interested in making their mark in the growing trading card community, visit replaysportscards.com/franchise for more information.

ABOUT REPLAY SPORTS CARDS
Replay Sports Cards is the first-ever sports card shop franchise, offering a full-service experience that includes buying, selling, trading and grading. With three shops across the U.S. and a strong presence at major card shows nationwide, Replay delivers an approachable, trustworthy environment for collectors of all ages and experience levels. The franchise is designed to make card collecting accessible, exciting, and meaningful, blending modern retail with a deep love for the hobby. Originally founded as One Stop Sports, Replay Sports Cards combines deep industry knowledge with a community-first mindset, both in-shop and through weekly livestreams on Whatnot (@ReplaySportsCards) and TikTok, (@ReplaySportsCards). To learn more, visit replaysportscards.com.

TURKU, FI / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Faron Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (HEL:FARON)(LSE:FARN)(AIM:FARN, First North:FARON), a global, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on creating innovative cancer treatments that leverage the patient's own immune system, today announces the following dates for the Company's financial reporting in 2027:

3 MarchFinancial statement release for the full year 2026 and Annual Report 2026 including financial statements for the full year
26 AugustHalf-year financial report for the period January 1 to June 30, 2027

The Annual General Meeting is planned to be held on 30 March 2027. A separate stock exchange notice will be issued by Faron's Board of Directors to convene the meeting.

About bexmarilimab

Bexmarilimab is Faron's proprietary, investigational immunotherapy designed to overcome resistance to existing treatments and optimize clinical outcomes by targeting myeloid cell function. It binds to Clever-1, a receptor on immunosuppressive macrophages that helps cancer evade the immune system. By targeting Clever-1, bexmarilimab reprograms the tumor microenvironment to ignite a potent anti-tumor immune response.

About Faron Pharmaceuticals Ltd

Faron (AIM:FARN, First North:FARON) is a global, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, focused on tackling cancers via novel immunotherapies. Its mission is to bring the promise of immunotherapy to a broader population by uncovering novel ways to control and harness the power of the immune system. The Company's lead asset is bexmarilimab, a novel anti-Clever-1 humanized antibody, with the potential to remove immunosuppression of cancers through reprogramming myeloid cell function. Bexmarilimab is being investigated in Phase 1/2 clinical trials as a potential therapy for patients with hematological cancers and solid tumors in combination with other standard treatments. data.title: Immorta Bio Demonstrates "Serial Killing" of Senescent Cells by SenoMune™-0257-Stimulated T Cells
data.description:
Immorta Bio Demonstrates "Serial Killing" of Senescent Cells by SenoMune™-0257-Stimulated T Cells

Immorta Bio Demonstrates "Serial Killing" of Senescent Cells by SenoMune™-0257-Stimulated T Cells

PR Newswire

MIAMI, Nov. 20, 2026

Laboratory studies observed a single CD8+ T cell eliminate up to 11 senescent cells, with no detectable activity against tested non-senescent controls

MIAMI, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Immorta Bio, Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing therapies to restore youthful biology, today announced new laboratory findings involving SenoMune™-0257, its investigational nine-amino-acid senolytic peptide immunotherapy. In these experiments, peptide-stimulated CD8+ T cells repeatedly eliminated senescent cells; an individual T cell was observed killing up to 11 senescent target cells in succession, an immune mechanism known as "serial killing."

The findings highlight two important properties for the development of potent senolytic peptide immunotherapy: the ability of an activated T cell to kill senescent targets repeatedly, and selectivity for senescent cells over the non-senescent controls tested. The experiments were conducted in vitro. SenoMune™-0257 has also entered human clinical evaluation, where investigators will assess its biological activity, including whether—and to what degree—it reduces senescent-cell burden in patients.

Senescent cells, sometimes called "zombie cells," accumulate with age and can contribute to chronic inflammation, tissue damage, and a range of age-related diseases. Immorta Bio is developing SenoMune™-0257 as a potent senolytic immunotherapy aimed at reducing this harmful cellular burden. The broader objective is to restore youthful biology and use it as a therapeutic engine for treating diseases of aging and, ultimately, aging itself.

"What stands out is the combination of potency and selectivity: in our laboratory experiments, a single CD8+ T cell repeatedly eliminated senescent targets while the non-senescent controls tested were spared," said Thomas E. Ichim, PhD, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Immorta Bio. "We have now moved SenoMune™-0257 into a pilot human study. An important focus is to determine whether the peptide reduces senescent-cell burden in patients, and how substantial that reduction may be."

The new SenoMune™-0257 findings build on Immorta Bio's published research into senolytic immunotherapy and offer additional mechanistic evidence supporting the company's strategy of clearing harmful senescent cells as a means of restoring youthful biology.

Human clinical evaluation of SenoMune™-0257 began on October 29, 2026, in an independent investigator-initiated pilot study in Mexico involving up to six patients with advanced cancer. The study is evaluating safety and seeking preliminary evidence of the peptide's biological activity, including whether—and to what extent—SenoMune™-0257 reduces senescent-cell burden in humans. The new laboratory findings and the ongoing human study represent complementary steps in the company's clinical development program.

"Restoring youthful biology is the central mission of Immorta Bio," said Boris N. Reznik, PhD, Chairman and CEO. "Clearing harmful senescent cells is one of our two fundamental therapeutic approaches, alongside restoring regenerative capacity through StemCellRevivify™. The ability of SenoMune™-0257–stimulated immune cells to repeatedly eliminate senescent cells in the laboratory is particularly exciting as we advance our first clinical evaluation and pursue a broader therapeutic engine for diseases of aging."

About Immorta Bio

Immorta Bio, Inc. is developing two complementary therapeutic platforms aimed at fundamental drivers of aging: SenoMune™, designed for immune-mediated clearance of senescent cells, and StemCellRevivify™, focused on restoring youthful regenerative capacity. Together, the platforms support the company's strategy of "Restoring Youthful Biology as a Therapeutic Engine" and its mission of "Treating Diseases of Aging and Treating Aging as Disease™."

Scientific background

Ichim TE et al. "Reduction of solid tumors by senescent cell immunization." Journal of Translational Medicine (2025). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12661736/. This publication concerns earlier preclinical senolytic-immunotherapy research, not the newly reported serial-killing experiment.

data.title: Arrive AI's Pro Forma Stockholders' Equity Now Above Nasdaq Minimum Requirement Following Recent Transactions
data.description:
INDIANAPOLIS, IN / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Arrive AI (NASDAQ:ARAI), a physical AI and autonomous logistics infrastructure company enabling drones, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), autonomous vehicles (AVs) and human couriers to securely exchange goods, today announced that, after giving pro forma effect to transactions completed since September 30, 2026, its stockholders' equity is approximately $7.7 million. This exceeds the $2.5 million minimum stockholders' equity required for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(b)(1). In its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q filed on November 13, the Company reported total stockholders' equity of $2,198,652 as of September 30, 2026. Since September 30, 2026, the Company has completed the following transactions:

  • Private placement: On October 5, 2026, the Company completed a private placement with an accredited investor for gross proceeds of $250,000.
  • At-The-Market program: As discussed on the Company's November 13, 2026 earnings call, the Company has raised approximately $1.3 million through its At-The-Market program since September 30, 2026.
  • Streeterville exchange: On November 19, 2026, the Company exchanged all of the outstanding debt owed to Streeterville Capital, LLC for preferred stock. The exchange removed the convertible note payable, accrued interest, unamortized discount and debt issuance costs, and related derivative liabilities that were carried at approximately $4.0 million on the Company's September 30, 2026 balance sheet.

Pro forma stockholders' equity (unaudited)

Total stockholders' equity, September 30, 2026 (as reported)$2,198,652
Private placement, net of expenses$245,000
At-the-market sales, net of offering costs$1,275,426
Streeterville exchange, removal of note payable, accrued interest, unamortized discount and debt issuance costs, and derivative liabilities$3,963,357
Pro forma total stockholders' equity$7,682,435

The pro forma information is unaudited. It assumes the transactions above were completed on September 30, 2026, and it reflects the Company's preliminary assessment of the accounting for them, including its expectation that the preferred stock will be classified as permanent stockholders' equity. It does not reflect the Company's operating results or any other events after September 30, 2026. The final accounting for the Streeterville exchange has not been completed.

The Company's stockholders' equity will change as it reports future results, and there can be no assurance that the Company will maintain compliance with the stockholders' equity requirement or any other Nasdaq listing requirement.

About Arrive AI

Arrive AI (NASDAQ:ARAI) is building the infrastructure for autonomous logistics through a network of intelligent delivery endpoints that enable secure, asynchronous exchange of goods. The company's platform supports drones, ground robotics, and human couriers, solving the "last inch of the last-mile" challenge across logistics, healthcare, and enterprise delivery.

data.title: THE GALA BY WE ARE ALL HUMAN HONORS LATINO LEADERSHIP AND LEGACY, AND INDUCTS VISIONARY MARKETERS INTO THE CMO HALL OF FAME
data.description:
THE GALA BY WE ARE ALL HUMAN HONORS LATINO LEADERSHIP AND LEGACY, AND INDUCTS VISIONARY MARKETERS INTO THE CMO HALL OF FAME

THE GALA BY WE ARE ALL HUMAN HONORS LATINO LEADERSHIP AND LEGACY, AND INDUCTS VISIONARY MARKETERS INTO THE CMO HALL OF FAME

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026

The sixth annual Gala honored Willy Chavarria, Mark D. Levine, Bea Perez, Henry R. Muñoz III, and inducted marketing leaders Leandro Barreto, Diego Scotti and Monica Gil.

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- We Are All Human celebrated its sixth annual Gala at Cipriani Wall Street; a night dedicated to elevating the Hispanic narrative, celebrating Latinos as an incredible economic force, and honoring those who believe and contribute to our community.

More than 450 leaders from business, media, philanthropy, fashion, and culture gathered to recognize incredible Latino trailblazers Willy Chavarria, CEO and Creative Director of Willy Chavarria; Mark D. Levine, New York City Comptroller; Bea Perez, Executive Vice President and Global Chief Communications, Sustainability and Strategic Partnerships Officer at The Coca-Cola Company, and Chair of The Coca-Cola Foundation; and Henry R. Muñoz III, American Activist and Founder & CEO of Cultural Productions.

"Soy Pocho. I am Chicano. Mexican-American [...] I stand here today as a leader in the global fashion industry. And I know that my place at that table means something far greater than my own success. Because we come from generous people. We don't just want a seat at the table. We want to make that table a whole lot bigger and with great food," said Willy Chavarria, CEO and Creative Director of Willy Chavarria.

"The very mission of this organization is to empower others by being a person for others to look towards the future, by never forgetting those of us who may never be in a room like this," said Henry R. Muñoz III, American Activist and Founder & CEO of Cultural Productions. "We share both the dream and the burden. I accept this recognition for all of the everyday heroes amongst us. The movement of a people begins with the steps of just one person, and the change that moves humanity forward is usually created by people whose names we will never know, people who decide to stand up for each other."

A special highlight of the night was Cirque Du Soleil performance was a tribute to quiet strength of encouragement, and the beauty of achieving the impossible together. The evening was honored by fabulous special guests including: Will Hernández (NFL Player), Cristo Fernández (Soccer Player, and Actor known for his role on Ted Lasso), Paloma Fernández, Kristin Genovese, Mary Nuñez, Bianca Peters, Teffi Pessoa, Jessica Torres, Valeria Villalobos, Jackie G, Samantha Camara, Aidee Chavez, Ross Pino, Mafer Salinas, and Honey German.

The evening marked the continuation of the CMO Hall of Fame, presented by Gabriel de Alba (Founder and Managing Partner, GDA Luma Capital Management, L.P.). This year's inductees included Monica Gil, (Chief Administrative & Marketing Officer NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises), Leandro Barreto (Global Chief Marketing Officer, Unilever and Beauty & Wellbeing, Unilever) and Diego Scotti (PayPal, Verizon, J.Crew, Condé Nast, American Express), honoring visionary marketing leaders redefining cultural relevance through inclusive storytelling.

"We have true momentum and true responsibility to consolidate a strong Latino brand that will allow the next generation to play the role we were always meant to play," said Claudia Romo Edelman, Founder and Executive Chair of We Are All Human. "It is possible, as Dolores Huerta said on this same stage a few years ago: ¡SÍ SE PUEDE!"

The Gala also featured heartfelt beneficiary testimonials from individual members, including Dr. Valery Maya (Chief of Staff, Zocalo Health & Chief Strategy Officer, NHHRI), Hervert Méndez (Director, Procurement AI & Transformation, MassMutual), and Dr. Cyndie Navarro-Dávila (Director, State & Local Campaigns - Health Equity, American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network), who shared how the organization's support empowered their professional journeys and helped them believe in their own superpowers.

Gala Co-Chairs included Gabriel de Alba (Founder & Managing Partner of GDA Luma Capital Management), Karla Martínez de Salas (Chief Content Officer, AVANCE and Editor-in-Chief New Lifestyle Media Brand), Bing Chen (CEO & Co-Founder, Gold House), and Marissa Solis (SVP Global Brand and Consumer Marketing, NFL).

The Gala surpassed its fundraising goals to support We Are All Human's mission. The live auction, led by renowned auctioneer Jacqueline Towers-Perkins, inspired guests to give generously in support of the cause.

Photos of the evening are available via BFA and Flickr.

The 2026 Gala was made possible thanks to the generous support of our corporate members and sponsors, led by the Presenting donor, L'Oreal. The organization extends their deepest gratitude to GDA Luma and Pat McGrath Labs®, Macquarie Group, Brown Rudnick, Aeromexico / Delta, Avance (Gary Acosta), Baker Tilly, Bayer, BMS (Bristol Myers Squibb), Sotol Romo, Cabrera Capital, The Coca-Cola Company, Edelman, Del Rey Express, Garcia Hamilton & Associates, EFE, Financial Times (FT), FP (Foreign Policy), Hispanic Scholarship Fund, Ketsali, iHeart Media, Macmillan Publishers, Paul Hastings, Rate, Reddit, Unilever, Salesforce, Nielsen, NFL, Pillsbury Law, Sotol Romo, Wall Street Journal (WSJ), Aeromexico, Avocados From Mexico, NGL Mitú, Bloomberg Philanthropies, Carter Ledyard, Horizon Media, LinkedIn,JC Gonzalez (GM Integritas Consulting), JM Smucker, Lerma, Mastercard, Mauricio Gutierrez, McKinsey, NBC Telemundo, Monarca Food Solutions, PwC, Walgreens, American Cancer Society, Azar Design, Canela Media, Liberty Mutual, Lowes, McDonalds, CROING and USTA.

data.title: These 5 defense stocks are drawing millions in insider bets ahead of military-spending boom in 2027
data.description:
By Michael Brush

U.S. defense spending is projected to be around $1.15 trillion next year, boosting business for companies that make missiles, drones, aircraft and more

A Tomahawk missile is fired from the guided-missile destroyer USS Thomas Hudner in March. Replenishments of missile systems will be a key focus of U.S. military spending in 2027.

When conflicts break out, so do concerns about war profiteering.

But making money in defense stocks during wartime can be harder than you might think. Not even some of the best experts around - defense-company insiders - always succeed.

Since the war with Iran began on Feb. 28, insiders at seven mid-sized defense-sector companies plowed millions of dollars into their shares. As of the close Nov. 12, they were collectively down 2.2%. If you simply bought the S&P 500 SPX the day after the war started, you'd be up 10.4% - much better than these defense insiders.

But that doesn't tell the whole story. Most of these defense-sector losses came from ill-timed purchases in two defense-related initial public offerings. Excluding these two big losers, where insider buyers were down 32% and 57%, defense-sector insiders are up 14.5%.

That's 28 percentage points better than the 14% decline in the iShares US Aerospace & Defense exchange traded fund ITA since the day after the war. It also seriously beats the S&P 500.

Below, I offer a guide to who is buying what in the defense sector, and medium-term developments which may further help insiders.

Zooming out, they should get a boost from 2027 defense-sector spending. You might think the Democratic takeover of the House and the Senate is bad news for defense spending. But that's wrong.

"Historically, defense spending is bipartisan," Gabelli Commercial Aerospace and Defense ETF GCAD manager Tony Bancroft told me in an interview. Defense spending is driven by geopolitical instability and the threat of war. Of course, there is a voter angle, as well. "A lot of constituents have exposure to the defense industry," he notes. Liberal California has a big defense presence, for example.

Sector analysts I spoke with project $1.15 trillion in defense-sector spending in 2027, or around 15% more than the prior year. Expect an emphasis on the "Golden Dome for America" missile-defense system, shipbuilding and, obviously, replenishment of missile systems like the Patriot, Tomahawk and terminal high-altitude area defense (THAAD) weapons.

"I don't think replenishing inventories will be a political football," Thomas Plumb, chief investment officer at Wisconsin Capital Management, told me in an interview. Defense companies with exposure to these line items should do well.

Karman

In mid-September, three directors at Karman (KRMN) put over $1 million into the stock at an average price of around $37.30. They were recently up over 8%. Insiders should see more gains from here because Karman is in so many areas prioritized in the budget.

For example, the company is big in missile defense (THAAD and Tomahawk components, among others).

"Karman stands out because replenishing our stockpiles of munitions is priority number one or two in the U.S. military," says Jason Leblang, who covers aerospace and defense for T. Rowe Price. Karman also makes components used in space programs, and for submarines, unmanned underwater vessels and tactical surface ships - all key to managing geopolitical tensions with China. Because Karman is in so many businesses prioritized in the defense budget, the company should see significant growth for at least the rest of the decade, Leblang told me in an interview.

BETA Technologies

A director at this electric-aircraft company bought $753,000 worth of stock in mid-May and early September at an average cost of around $17.60. He was recently up 43% on the purchases. The company blew away third-quarter estimates by reporting 98% revenue gains linked to increased sales of aircraft components and charging-station equipment.

BETA Technologies (BETA) is less of a defense company than it used to be. Defense-related revenue has fallen to under 10% of overall sales, down from 30% or more in recent years. I still consider it a defense company because it's looking for defense-related growth.

In September, it showed off one of its electric aircraft at the largest military aircraft show in the U.S., called the Miramar Air Show. "We were the first electric aircraft to fly at that military air show," founder and CEO Kyle Clark said in the third-quarter earnings call. "The response we are hearing from the defense community is direct and consistent. There is an existing capability gap we can fill."

Honeywell Aerospace

A director here put $1 million into this stock at $156 in early September. He was recently up over 6%.

A spinoff from Honeywell International (HON), Honeywell Aerospace (HONA) makes key components used in aircraft, like cockpit electronics, auxiliary power units and motion-control systems. So, it will benefit as the military upgrades its aircrafts with programs like the F/A-XX fighter jet and the F-47, notes Bancroft, the Gabelli portfolio manager. Around 59% of revenue comes from commercial aircraft-related sales, so this is not a pure defense play.

Loar

Three insiders put $8.4 million into this stock at around $64.20 in mid-March. They were recently up over 16%.

Loar (LOAR) sells aerospace and defense aircraft components like braking and de-icing systems, and flight controls. Like Honeywell, Loar is not a pure defense play. About 75% of revenue is linked to commercial aircraft production. But it will benefit from defense-spending growth, and Leblang at T. Rowe Price is bullish on commercial aircraft demand. He thinks the sector is still in the early stages of a long demand upcycle. Factors like a rising middle class, especially in Asia, and the need for more for fuel-efficient aircraft are driving demand.

Parsons

Parsons (PSN) helps governments around the world with a wide array of defense-related issues from cybersecurity and electronic warfare to missile systems. It also helps build infrastructure like airports, highways and transit systems.

Three directors and the CEO put $3 million into this stock in May and early August at around $50. They were recently down 2%, but they could do well from here.

Parsons stock got hit hard in late July when the company reported a 1% decline in second-quarter sales. The company took a slew of charges and write-offs in what might have been a "kitchen sink" moment, says Leblang. Down here (the shares are off 41% in the past year) he thinks the stock has gotten very cheap. The 0.8 price-to-sales ratio is a 29% discount to the trailing five-year average of 1.2, according to LSEG.

This could be a turning point. Third-quarter revenue growth turned positive, advancing 2%. The proposed defense-budget emphasis on missile defense, cybersecurity, space programs, electronic warfare and base modernization plays to Parsons' strengths, CEO Carey Smith said in the third-quarter earnings call.

Two IPO losers

Aevex

A cluster of insiders at drone maker Aevex (AVEX), including the CEO and CFO, put around $1.5 million into the stock for its IPO in April. They were recently down over 30%. The knock on this company is that drone production is a crowded space. Bulls counter that while the company does have exposure to the crowded small-drone space, its core focus is more complex drones that have high barriers to entry. Drones are also a budget priority.

"The government has a number of big programs designed to kickstart the U.S. manufacturing base, and it is doing it in lightning speed," Needham Aggressive Growth Fund manager John Barr told me in an interview.

Applied Aerospace & Defense

Insiders at this aircraft and rocket component maker (AADX) put over $1.1 million into the stock at $20 in its early June IPO. They are now down over 65%. The stock has gotten punished because the company cut its sales guidance. On the bright side, the company has a nearly $1.3 billion order backlog, which is twice the trailing 12-month revenue.

Michael Brush is a columnist for MarketWatch. At the time of publication, he held shares of LOAR. Brush has suggested LOAR in his stock newsletter, Brush Up on Stocks. Follow him on X @mbrushstocks

-Michael Brush

Investor Alert: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of the FMC Corporation Class Action Lawsuit

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP informs investors that a class action was filed on behalf of all persons who purchased or otherwise acquired FMC Corporation (NYSE: FMC) common stock between February 4, 2026 and October 14, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). FMC Corporation is an agricultural sciences company, develops, markets, and sells crop protection chemicals in Latin America, North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia.

The complaint alleges that FMC misled investors regarding its 2026 financial outlook

Investors who purchased FMC Corporation common stock during the Class Period and suffered significant losses should contact Robbins LLP before January 19, 2027 for information about the lawsuit.

Why Was FMC Sued?

According to the complaint, during the Class Period, defendants created the false impression that they possessed reliable information pertaining to the Company’s projected 2026 financial outlook and anticipated recovery, based on projected growth in its core portfolio, Rynaxypyr and new active ingredients, as well as manufacturing cost reductions and improved inventory management.

In truth, the Company was seeing a significant distributor inventory problem, in which elevated-priced inventory held by distributors was difficult to sell thereby impairing replenishment orders across FMC’s portfolio and threatening the Company’s ability to generate new sales, revenue, EBITDA and cash flow, making FMC’s full year 2026 financial outlook unlikely to be met.

Plaintiff alleges that defendants misled investors by providing the public with materially flawed statements of confidence in cost savings and growth projections, which did not account for these variables.

Why Did FMC Stock Drop?

The complaint alleges that the truth emerged on October 14, 2026, when FMC announced preliminary third quarter 2026 results materially below expectations and sharply reduced adjusted EBITA for the quarter.

On this news, the price of FMC’s common stock declined from a closing market price of $8.09 per share on October 14, 2026, to $5.62 per share on October 15, 2026, a decline of about 31%.

What Can FMC Investors Do Now?

Investors who purchased FMC Corporation common stock during the Class Period may be eligible to serve as lead plaintiff. The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Shareholders who wish to seek appointment as lead plaintiff should contact Robbins LLP before the January 19, 2027 deadline for information about the appointment process.

Shareholders do not need to serve as lead plaintiff to share in any potential recovery. Those who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis, with no upfront or out-of-pocket fees or expenses.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the FMC Corporation securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP represents investors in securities fraud and shareholder derivative litigation. We have helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history.

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

data.title: Bank of America strategist warns doom loop could hit stocks with Wall Street underpricing hard-landing risks
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

A hard landing could trigger a "doom loop" for stocks, warns one Wall Street strategist.

The S&P 500 is nearing a level worth buying if the U.S. avoids a recession, but one strategist warns Wall Street is underpricing the risk of a hard landing, saying investors should wait before buying risky assets.

Strategists led by Michael Hartnett said if the Fed is still Wall Street's best friend and corporate credit and the S&P 500 continue to slide, market turmoil will "short-circuit" the Fed rate-hike cycle. But if the Fed is now an "inflation tough guy" after the midterms, the hard-landing risks grow.

Hartnett's comments come amid increasingly hawkish central-bank commentary, with St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem talking of the need for as many as four rate increases by the spring. Fed governor Christopher Waller has said the central bank should consider a half-point rate rise in December.

An S&P 500 SPX below 7,000, in a soft-landing scenario where the U.S. avoids a recession, would be a buy, he said.

The S&P 500 closed Thursday at 7,175.83, now more than 2% below its 200-day average. Stock-market futures (ES00) pointed to a weaker start on Friday.

Bank of America's own fund-manager survey, released Tuesday, showed half the investors they polled thought there would be a soft landing and 42% expected no landing at all, i.e. continued or accelerating growth. Only 3% expected a recession. "We say hard landing likelihood too low," said Hartnett.

He said he fears a doom loop, where once estimates of GDP and earnings per share are reduced, stock-market allocations are cut, and investors only sell what they own. For now, investors are "hiding" in low-volatility and defensive stocks, he said.

Investors should wait until the narrative flips from Fed hikes to Fed cuts, then buy "cyclicals Cs" - crypto, chips, copper, consumer and condos.

-Steve Goldstein
